To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the DNA adducts of carcinogens have been identified, (b) the DNA addducts of carcinogens are formed in the target tissue, (c) DNA adducts are formed at the sites of mutation, (d) DNA adduct formation is a cause of mutation, and (e) DNA adduct levels correlate with cancer incidence.
the DNA adducts of carcinogens are mutagens and the mutagenic activity of carcinogens is related to their carcinogenic activity.
DNA adducts are the cause of cancer, the DNA damage caused by adducts is the mutation, and the mutation is the cause of cancer.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and quantification of DNA adductsin human tissues and cells, and with the relationship of DNA damage to the initiation and progression of human cancer.
the chemical causes of cancer.
the chemical modification of DNA by electrophilic carcinogens, and the consequences of such modifications for DNA replication and repair.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the identification of DNA as the target for carcinogenic agents has been a long and arduous process (6).
'DNA damage, especially DNA adduct formation, is an essential step in the initiation of cancer' (6).
'chemical causes of cancer are a fact' (6).
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we are now able to identify DNA adducts of many carcinogens, and that we can identify the DNA adducts that are formed in the human population, and we are now able, in principle, to identify DNA addducts that are formed _in vivo_ in humans.
the development of ideas has been from a 'one adduct-one disease' to the 'one disease-one adduct' concept (6).
we started with the idea of a chemical cause of cancer, and ended with the idea of the chemical cause of cancer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
DNA damage is a necessary condition for cancer, but not a sufficient one.
the DNA adducts of the ultimate carcinogens are formed in the body and not in the test tube.
DNA adducts can indeed lead to cancer.
